column1: # CPU microarchitecture lookup, keyed on what /proc/cpuinfo actually reports.
#   vendor  family  model  microarchitecture  launched  process  gen
#   model   decimal, matching "model"; * matches any model in the family
#   launched  year the microarchitecture shipped, not the year this part did
#   gen     ordinal into cpu-generations.tsv, or - for a part that is not on the
#           consumer generation ladder (Xeon Scalable, EPYC) or whose microarchitecture
#           spans two generations without the model number distinguishing them
# Keying on family/model rather than the marketing string is the whole point: "13th Gen
# Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1360P" tells you a generation, 6/186 tells you Raptor Lake, and
# the same silicon ships under several names. Rows are added as parts are confirmed; an
# unmatched CPU prints its model string alone rather than a guess.
# Data as of: 2026-08-01. Confirm additions against Intel ARK or AMD's product pages —
# the family/model pair is printed by `lscpu` and by this tool under --debug.
# * rows are the fallback for a family and must sort after specific models; the lookup
# takes the first exact match, then the family wildcard.
# Note Raptor Lake: models 183 and 191 cover both 13th and 14th Gen, because 14th Gen
# desktop is the same silicon refreshed. The table says 13; the model *string* says
# "14th Gen" when it is one, and the string wins. See hwdata_cpu_generation.
